description: The template contract: every {{TOKEN}} and kit:if flag a template may use. The render script fills tokens from detect and the owner's answers and fails on any token that is unknown, unfilled or does not match its type. See docs/templates.md in the kit repo.

string.description: One line of prose. No braces, angle brackets or backticks, so a value can't open a token, a tag or a code span.

identifier.description: A name such as a branch prefix or owner/repo. Safe in shell, YAML and Markdown.

path.description: A repo-relative path. No leading slash, no '..'.

command.description: One command line with no shell metacharacters (no quotes, $, ;, |, &, redirects or globs), so it can be matched exactly by a guard.

json-array.description: A JSON array of strings, inserted as a literal. Its name ends in _JSON and it has no twin. Each item must match the token itemPattern. Used only in .mjs and .json templates.

rejectCommandPatterns.description: A value is rejected at render time if any command in it (a command token, an item of VERIFY_COMMANDS_JSON or DB_COMMANDS_JSON, or the command inside a Bash(...) rule) matches one of these. The production list is a backstop (remote hosts, deploy CLIs, connection URLs, push, deploy and release scripts); it is not the classifier, so a match means: ask the owner, never allow. The blockedByGuard list is what bash-guard blocks anyway (inline env assignments, git --output), so such an entry could never run. The first-word patterns also match behind one runner word (for example `npx <tool>` or `<runner> exec <tool>`); deeper wrappers such as `bash -c` are not unwrapped, which the command type's no-quotes rule already blocks. The installed .claude/hooks/guards.test.mjs and .agents/hooks/agy-guard.mjs carry a copy of the production list (minus host names the kit lint keeps out of templates); the kit lint checks they stay in sync.

OWNER.description: The human who approves plans and merges. No "|", because it appears in Markdown tables.

ENV_PREFIX.description: Prefix of the pre-push override variable, <ENV_PREFIX>_ALLOW_PUSH_MAIN.
ENV_PREFIX.source: derived from PROJECT_NAME, confirmed by the owner

KIT_VERSION.description: The kit version that rendered the files.

CMD_CHECKS.description: The detected check commands (typecheck, lint, test, in that order) joined with ' && '.
CMD_CHECKS.source: derived from CMD_TYPECHECK, CMD_LINT and CMD_TEST
CMD_CHECKS.example: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test

CMD_HOOK_TESTS.description: The command that runs the harness's own script tests: one quoted glob per installed module that ships tests (.claude/hooks for claude, .agents/hooks for antigravity, .agents/skills/*/scripts for skills such as open-pr, .githooks for the pre-push guard).

DB_PATH.description: The folder holding the schema and migrations, which the architect may edit. No segment may start with a dot, so it can never be the repo root, .git/ or .claude/.

PERSONA_NAME_BUILDER.description: Display name of the main session (the builder).

PERSONA_NAME_ARCHITECT.description: Display name of the architect persona.

PERSONA_NAME_PLANNER.description: Display name of the planner persona.

PERSONA_NAME_REVIEWER.description: Display name of the reviewer persona.

PERSONA_NAME_RETRO.description: Display name of the retro persona.

PERSONA_NAME_RESEARCHER.description: Display name of the researcher persona.

PERSONA_NAME_PM.description: Display name of the pm (product manager) persona.

VERIFY_COMMANDS_JSON.description: The exact check commands (CMD_TYPECHECK, CMD_LINT, CMD_TEST that exist, in that order). bash-guard and agy-guard allow each one, for the read-only and architect profiles. May be empty.
VERIFY_COMMANDS_JSON.source: derived from CMD_TYPECHECK, CMD_LINT and CMD_TEST

DB_COMMANDS_JSON.description: The exact local-database commands the architect may run (generate, create a migration without applying it, apply to the local database, seed). Never a command that reaches a deployed database.
DB_COMMANDS_JSON.source: detect, then classified and confirmed by the owner

ALLOW_RULES_JSON.description: permissions.allow entries for .claude/settings.json: git basics plus the local commands in .agents/rules/commands.md. Never a production-reaching command.

GH_REPO.description: The GitHub repo, owner/name, that open-pr opens PRs against.

GH_ACCOUNT.description: The gh account whose token open-pr passes per command (gh auth token --user <account>), so the active account never has to change.

DATE_YM.description: Year and month of the install, for plan file names. The only token allowed in a template path.

RISKY_PATHS_JSON.description: Paths whose change needs a Rollback line in the PR Notes. An entry ending in / is a folder prefix; any other entry is a file name matched at any depth. A folder entry must end in /: without it, the entry only matches a file of that name.
RISKY_PATHS_JSON.source: detect (CI workflows, container and deploy files, schema folder), confirmed by the owner

PM_TOOL.description: The PM tool that holds the backlog, reached through its MCP server. The installer suggests Linear; Notion, Jira, GitHub Issues and others work the same way. Without a tool (has.pmTool false) the backlog is docs/backlog.md.

PM_SCOPE.description: Where this project's items live in the PM tool (a project, team, board or database), so the pm persona never touches other projects' items in a shared workspace.
PM_SCOPE.example: the Example App project in team ENG

VERIFY_DOCKERFILE.description: The Dockerfile that builds the production image, for smoke-local and e2e-verify --docker.
VERIFY_DOCKERFILE.source: detect (Dockerfile, .env.example, package scripts), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_APP_PORT.description: The port the app listens on inside the production container.
VERIFY_APP_PORT.source: detect (Dockerfile, .env.example, package scripts), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_HEALTH_PATH.description: The path that answers 200 once the app is up (a health route, or / when there is none).
VERIFY_HEALTH_PATH.source: detect (a health route in the source), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_DB_ENGINE.description: The throwaway database the verify skills start: postgres, or none for an app without one.
VERIFY_DB_ENGINE.source: detect (Dockerfile, .env.example, package scripts), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_DB_IMAGE.description: The image of the throwaway database, matching production's major version.
VERIFY_DB_IMAGE.source: detect (Dockerfile, .env.example, package scripts), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_DB_URL_ENV.description: The env var the app reads its database URL from.
VERIFY_DB_URL_ENV.source: detect (Dockerfile, .env.example, package scripts), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_SECRET_ENV_JSON.description: Env vars that get a fake secret when the verify skills boot the app (auth secrets, signing keys).
VERIFY_SECRET_ENV_JSON.source: detect (.env.example names with SECRET, KEY or TOKEN), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_LOCAL_URL_ENV_JSON.description: Env vars that get the local app URL (http://localhost:<port>) when the verify skills boot the app.
VERIFY_LOCAL_URL_ENV_JSON.source: detect (Dockerfile, .env.example, package scripts), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_BUILD_ARG_URL_JSON.description: Docker build args that get the local app URL, for URLs baked into the client bundle at build time.
VERIFY_BUILD_ARG_URL_JSON.source: detect (Dockerfile, .env.example, package scripts), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_EXTRA_ENV_JSON.description: Fixed NAME=value pairs the app needs to boot locally. Never a secret or a URL: no spaces, colons or @.
VERIFY_EXTRA_ENV_JSON.source: detect (Dockerfile, .env.example, package scripts), confirmed by the owner

VERIFY_CONTAINER_MIGRATE_JSON.description: Commands run in a one-off container of the production image before it boots, for images whose entrypoint doesn't migrate. Empty when the entrypoint does.
VERIFY_CONTAINER_MIGRATE_JSON.source: detect (the Dockerfile entrypoint), confirmed by the owner

SMOKE_SECOND_BOOT.description: Whether smoke-local boots the image a second time on the same database, proving migrations are a no-op and the seed re-runs.

SMOKE_MUST_FAIL_WITHOUT_JSON.description: Required secrets: a boot without each one must fail, never answer 200.

E2E_MODE.description: How e2e-verify serves the app by default: the production build on the host (fast), or the production image (full parity).

E2E_SETUP_JSON.description: Host commands that prepare the throwaway database for e2e-verify (migrate, seed). Local only: the database URL points at the throwaway container.
E2E_SETUP_JSON.source: detect (package scripts), confirmed by the owner

E2E_BUILD_JSON.description: Host commands that build the production app for e2e-verify.
E2E_BUILD_JSON.source: detect (package scripts), confirmed by the owner

E2E_START_JSON.description: The one host command that serves the built app for e2e-verify (empty only in docker mode). It gets PORT; see E2E_START_PORT_ARGS_JSON when it ignores it.
E2E_START_JSON.source: detect (package scripts), confirmed by the owner

E2E_START_PORT_ARGS_JSON.description: Flags e2e-verify puts before the port on the start command, for servers that ignore PORT (for example --port). Empty when PORT works.
E2E_START_PORT_ARGS_JSON.source: detect (package scripts), confirmed by the owner

E2E_TEST_COMMAND.description: The command that runs the E2E suite. It reads E2E_BASE_URL and E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR.
E2E_TEST_COMMAND.source: detect (test runner config), confirmed by the owner

BACKUP_ENGINE.description: The production database engine db-backup dumps. Only postgres is supported.

BACKUP_NAME.description: A lowercase slug for dump file names and the default backup folder (~/Backups/<name>/db).
BACKUP_NAME.source: derived from PROJECT_NAME, confirmed by the owner

BACKUP_ENV_FILE.description: The repo-relative, git-ignored env file the owner puts the production URL in. Only the db-backup script reads it.

BACKUP_URL_ENV_JSON.description: Variable names in the backup env file to take the production URL from, in order.

BACKUP_DIR_ENV.description: The env var that overrides the backup folder.
BACKUP_DIR_ENV.source: derived from ENV_PREFIX, confirmed by the owner

DB_PROVIDER.description: Where the production database is hosted, by name, for db-backup's instructions.

DB_PROVIDER_MCP.description: The name of the database host provider's MCP server, as the owner connected it.

has.db.description: The repo owns a database schema or migrations.

has.ui.description: The project has a user-facing UI.

has.container.description: A container image is the production artifact.

has.checks.description: At least one of has.typecheck, has.lint and has.test.

module.claude.description: The claude adapter module is installed.

module.antigravity.description: The antigravity adapter module is installed.

flow.gitFlow.description: The repo uses Git Flow (a long-lived dev branch promoted to main).

has.pmTool.description: The backlog lives in an external PM tool reached through its MCP server. False means it lives in docs/backlog.md.

has.dbProviderMcp.description: The database host provider has an MCP server the owner connects with their own login; db-backup uses it read-only for checks that expose no credential.
